request.idea: The lighthouse keeper of a small coastal town has vanished, and the lighthouse now shines with a cold green light that lures ships onto the rocks.

seeds.text: The wind carries the smell of cinnamon from where nobody bakes.
The beast is a transformed member of the town council.
Torches and lanterns gutter out after a short while.
To regain a title stolen from the family.
A shoe that always walks home.

concept.title: The Stolen Name of the Light
concept.tagline: A green light promises safe harbour, and beneath the cliff the drowned demand their due.
concept.teaser: A smell of cinnamon drifts from Ugletoft’s empty lighthouse. The green beam of the light points in over the reef where the waves break white. Out in the dusk a cargo ship has just turned towards the light; the keeper has not been seen since noon.
concept.premise: Halfdan the lighthouse keeper is held prisoner beneath the lighthouse while a transformed town councillor uses an old salvaged lens to lure a ship aground. The party can follow witnesses, cargo papers or the lighthouse’s maintenance passage to him. Stopping the beam saves the ship; freeing Halfdan makes sure someone can light the true light again.
concept.truth: Councillor Gorm Krogh has found a genuine letter showing that his family was wrongly stripped of the hereditary title of light reeve. He paid smugglers to fetch a bronze mirror from his family’s wreck and burned cinnamon resin in its bowl to call up the drowned as witnesses. The mirror’s pact turned him into one of the undead and now demands a new wreck as payment. Halfdan discovered the deception; Gorm Krogh chained him to the mirror’s turning gear so that he could not reach the lever that turns the beam down into the floor. Gorm Krogh can still choose to break the pact, but he fears that nobody will hear his case if he gives up his only leverage.
concept.conflict: The documented wrong done to Gorm Krogh gives him no right to sacrifice a stranger’s ship. The smugglers want to cover up their own part, but they have no wish to become murdering wreckers.
concept.goal: Free Halfdan in the Mirror Chamber and stop the green beam before the cargo ship strikes the reef.

objective.state: Awake, exhausted and chained to the bronze mirror’s turning gear in the Mirror Chamber. He can talk and walk, but the short chain keeps him from the tilt lever. Gorm Krogh has the key on his belt.
objective.resolution: Physical route: lever the chain’s rusty wall bracket free with a crowbar or a sturdy bar; a DC 12 Strength (Athletics) check takes 1 minute. On a success Halfdan is free. On a failure the bracket is still stuck and the work has cost 5 minutes in all; the attempt can be repeated. Instead, the lock can be opened with thieves’ tools and a DC 12 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, with the same time and the same result on a failure, or with Gorm Krogh’s key without a check. Without a fight: show Gorm Krogh the proof of his family’s title, or let him read his letter aloud himself, and promise a public hearing of his case. A DC 12 Charisma (Persuasion) check makes him hand over the key; on a failure he will still do so if a hero signs the promise and lets him keep the original letter as security. The conversation takes 5 minutes, even on a failure. Once freed, Halfdan turns the tilt lever down at once, without a check; the party can also reach and turn it themselves while he is still chained. It takes an action, stops the beam and causes no damage. The normal light can be lit 10 minutes later. If the party only stops the beam, the ship is saved, but Halfdan must still be freed. When the deadline runs out, the ship strikes the reef if the beam still points out to sea; Halfdan does not die automatically and can be rescued afterwards.

concept.stakes: After 90 minutes the cargo ship strikes the reef if the green beam can still be seen from the sea. The hull splits, the cargo is lost and eight sailors are trapped on the wreck; they can still be rescued. Halfdan and Gorm Krogh stay in the Mirror Chamber unless the heroes change things.

clock.start: The party stands on Ugletoft’s quay. The green light is lit, and the cargo ship has just changed course towards the reef. Start the clock at zero here.

ticks.event: The ship passes the outermost seamark and sets her course straight for the light.
ticks.sign: Her two white lanterns now stand on either side of the green stripe of the light. Vibeke points out the wrong course; the beam can still be stopped in time.

ticks.event: The ship’s lead line finds less water than expected. The crew begin to shorten sail but still follow the false light.
ticks.sign: Three short horn blasts echo across the harbour. If the beam is put out or covered now, the ship can still turn clear.

ticks.event: If the beam still reaches the sea, the ship strikes the reef; the hull splits, the cargo is lost and eight sailors take refuge on the afterdeck. If the beam has been stopped, the ship stays clear of the reef and none of this happens.
ticks.sign: At the wreck, timber cracks and the ship’s bell tolls without pause. A rope made fast from the rock ledge can still be used to rescue the crew; time cannot give back the cargo.

clock.costs: From the quay to the customs shed: 5 minutes. From the quay straight to the rock ledge: 10 minutes. From the customs shed to the rock ledge: 10 minutes. From the rock ledge through the maintenance passage to the Mirror Chamber: 5 minutes. The same times back; no extra hidden travel time. An ordinary conversation or a thorough search of one place takes 5 minutes; necessary clues are found in that time without a check. Combat is counted in rounds, not automatically as 5 minutes. The special attempts at the lock and the conversation with Gorm Krogh have their times in the objective’s resolution. A Short Rest takes 1 hour; a Long Rest cannot fit before the deadline.
clock.deadline: 90 minutes after the party arrives at the quay, the ship strikes the reef, but only if the green beam can still be seen from the sea. Putting out or fully screening the beam before then ends the danger to the ship for good; the clock does not restart. Halfdan can be rescued after the deadline, even though the cargo is lost by then.

concept.twist: The undead creature in the Mirror Chamber is Councillor Gorm Krogh, and his letter about the stolen title of light reeve is genuine. The party can expose his crime and at the same time demand that the old wrong be looked into; the one does not cancel the other.
hooks: Thyra Bøgh once helped the party’s rogue get rid of a suspicious item. Now she asks for help getting Halfdan out of the caves and offers to own up to her own part if the keeper comes home alive.

Vibeke shows the party’s wizard a drawing of the rebuilt lighthouse mechanism. She would like a fellow expert’s opinion, but she is loath to admit that she approved the work without visiting the lighthouse.

villain.name: Gorm Krogh
villain.nature: A town councillor turned into one of the drowned undead; his face is wax-grey, and salt water runs from his dry sleeves.
villain.want: To have his family’s stolen title of light reeve publicly recognised, so that the family is no longer remembered as thieves.
villain.plan: Keep Halfdan at the mirror’s turning gear, hold the green beam until the ship arrives, and afterwards demand the town council’s signature as the price for stopping further wrecks. He stays in the Mirror Chamber the whole time; he does not yet know that the smugglers will testify against him.
villain.weakness: He knows that the letter is stronger proof than a murdered ship’s crew, and he still wants to be heard as a man. A public hearing and a written promise can make him hand over the key without a fight. The mirror’s tilt lever is within anyone’s reach; he has no magical power to restart it from afar.

cast.name: Gorm Krogh
cast.where: In the Mirror Chamber by the turning gear, with the key and his family’s original letter on his belt.

cast.name: Halfdan
cast.where: In the Mirror Chamber, chained to the mirror’s turning gear; awake and able to walk once freed.

cast.name: Thyra Bøgh
cast.role: Smuggler and the rogue’s old contact
cast.where: On Ugletoft’s quay by her dinghy. She stays there to keep the boat ready unless the party takes her along.

cast.name: Vibeke
cast.role: Harbour clerk with a knowledge of optics
cast.where: On Ugletoft’s quay with the key to the customs shed and her document folder. She unlocks the shed for the party and goes back to the quay; she is never in two places at once.

factions.name: The Quay Smugglers
factions.want: To stop a wreck without losing the dinghy and all their profit.
factions.method: They offer routes and testimony; Thyra Bøgh eats pickled onions to hide the smell of the cinnamon resin she has moved.
factions.attitude: Wary of being accused, but willing to help Halfdan. Asking questions never starts a fight by itself.

factions.name: The Drowned Witnesses
factions.want: To have their names read aloud from the salvage roll, and the mirror’s green beam put out.
factions.method: They stand guard at the desecrated memorial stone on the rock ledge; they gain no new magical powers beyond their ordinary SRD stat blocks.
factions.attitude: They let the party pass if the roll is read aloud with respect or their grave coins are put back at the stone.

outline.title: The Wrong Course
outline.purpose: Start the clock on the quay, meet the witnesses, and choose between the documents in the customs shed and the direct way to the rock ledge.

outline.title: A Letter with Two Seals
outline.purpose: An optional visit to the customs shed gives proof against Gorm Krogh, documents his family’s claim and makes a peaceful solution easier.

outline.title: The Names in the Salt Stone
outline.purpose: Reach the rock ledge, deal with the drowned guards and find the hidden maintenance passage, without locking progress behind a check.

outline.title: The Hand on the Lever
outline.purpose: Meet the transformed Gorm Krogh, free Halfdan and stop the mirror by negotiation, guile or combat; settle the outcome by the same clock.

clueMap.conclusion: Halfdan is in the Mirror Chamber beneath the lighthouse; the maintenance passage from the rock ledge leads there.

clues.observation: Without asking for payment, Thyra Bøgh tells them that she saw Halfdan go down the cliff stair with Gorm Krogh. She points out the mouth of the maintenance passage behind the memorial stone.
clues.inference: An eyewitness ties the missing keeper to a particular way in beneath the lighthouse.

clues.observation: Halfdan’s work note lies in Vibeke’s folder together with a simple maintenance drawing. It names the route and the turning gear.
clues.inference: The keeper’s own appointment places him at the mirror and gives the usable way there.
clues.handout:
To the harbour clerk.
I am going with Gorm Krogh to the Mirror Chamber beneath the lighthouse.
Way in from the rock ledge, behind the memorial stone; press the left-hand stone in.
The turning gear must be inspected before evening. — Halfdan

clues.observation: Through a crack behind the memorial stone Halfdan can be heard shouting that he is chained by the mirror. A metal bar scrapes uselessly against a lever.
clues.inference: The keeper is alive and trapped on the other side of the hidden passage.

clueMap.conclusion: Gorm Krogh ordered the false light and is himself the transformed creature at the mirror.

clues.observation: Thyra Bøgh shows her receipt for the bronze mirror and the cinnamon resin. Gorm Krogh’s full name and council seal stand beneath an instruction about the ship’s course.
clues.inference: His own order describes the deception; he is not merely the victim of someone else’s ritual.
clues.handout:
Received: one bronze mirror and cinnamon resin.
Place the mirror beneath the lighthouse; hold the green beam on the reef until the ship is in.
Payment upon my reinstatement as light reeve.
Gorm Krogh. [The town council’s wax seal]

clues.observation: A copy of Gorm Krogh’s handwritten pact letter names both his wish and the price: his living form as a pledge until the first wreck. Vibeke can compare the handwriting with the signed order without a check.
clues.inference: The same person ordered the false light and made the bargain that explains the transformation.
clues.handout:
I, Gorm Krogh, call the witnesses home.
Let my living form stand as pledge until the sea has its first wreck.
Then I shall claim back my family’s name and office.
No one else shall bear the blame for my choice.

clues.observation: Halfdan shouts through the crack: Gorm Krogh’s skin turned grey when the resin was lit; he still wore his signet ring and talked about his family’s title.
clues.inference: A living prisoner saw the transformation itself and identifies the man, not just a similar seal.

clueMap.conclusion: The green light can be stopped by turning the mirror down; Gorm Krogh can also be won over with the promise of a public hearing.

clues.observation: Vibeke shows a maintenance drawing of the mirror in its lowered position and explains that Halfdan always makes the light safe with the free tilt lever.
clues.inference: The mechanism has a simple safe position that needs neither a spell nor Gorm Krogh’s death.
clues.handout:
SAFE POSITION
Turn the tilt lever all the way down. The mirror then points at the stone floor.
Do not block the lever with cargo. No key is needed.

clues.observation: The old charter bears two genuine seals and grants the Krogh family the title of light reeve. On the cover Gorm Krogh has written that he will ask only for an open hearing, if anyone dares promise him one.
clues.inference: His claim can be tested with documents; a firm promise of a public hearing gives him a way out without more victims.
clues.handout:
The Krogh family bears the title of light reeve by lawful inheritance. [Two old seals]
On the cover, in a newer hand: Let me read this before an open council.
Give me a promise the town can hear, and I will not need the light.

clues.observation: Through the crack Halfdan explains that the lever is free; it is only he who is chained too short to reach it. He has heard Gorm Krogh rehearsing the words for his hearing.
clues.inference: Both solutions can be carried out in the Mirror Chamber, and the keeper can help at once when the chain is loose.

partyMoments.moment: The rogue knows Thyra Bøgh and can open Halfdan’s lock; the witness also reveals the hidden maintenance passage, so a failed search never stops the adventure.
The cleric can reconsecrate the desecrated memorial stone by reading the names on the salvage roll and putting the coins back. That makes the drowned guards peaceful without a fight.

The wizard can see through Vibeke’s old treatise on optics and question her approval. Magical light works in the passage, where hand-held torches and lanterns go out after one minute; the mirror’s turning gear needs no spell.
The fighter can break the chain’s wall bracket, hold a narrow passage against the drowned, or get the two quay guards to ready a rescue rope, without costing the party an extra trip.

scenes.title: The Wrong Course
scenes.summary: On Ugletoft’s quay a false light is steering the cargo ship towards the reef. Thyra Bøgh and Vibeke give the party concrete clues and a direct route to Halfdan; the documents can be examined first, but they are not a ticket to the rest of the adventure.
scenes.readAloud: The green stripe from the lighthouse cuts across black water and white surf. In front of you a dinghy creaks against the timbers of the quay; by its bow stands an open jar of pickled onions. The smell of cinnamon drifts down from the cliff, though the town’s bread oven is cold. Out at sea, two white ship’s lanterns turn slowly in towards the reef.
details: Start the clock at zero. Thyra Bøgh points at the ship’s course and says that Halfdan went down the cliff stair with Gorm Krogh around noon. She saw them disappear behind the memorial stone on the rock ledge. She shows the way for free, even if she does not know the party’s rogue.

Thyra Bøgh has made money fetching the bronze mirror and the cinnamon resin. The onions hide the smell on her breath, but not the resin under her nails. She shows her signed receipt when the party asks about the cargo. Hand out the receipt’s full text from the clue list: Gorm Krogh expressly ordered the beam to be held on the reef. She would rather testify than watch the ship sink.

Vibeke shows her folded maintenance drawing: the tilt lever can turn the mirror down to the stone floor without a key or magic. She also explains that a bright signal flag will not outshine the green light; putting out or covering the beam itself, on the other hand, makes the ship safe before the deadline. The drawing’s exact safety text is in the clue list and can be handed out now.

Vibeke has the key to the customs shed and her document folder. If the party asks for all the papers at once, A Letter with Two Seals can be played here on the quay with the folder; use that scene’s 5-minute search and skip the walk to the customs shed. There is no reason to hold back information that is already in her hand. Otherwise she walks the 5 minutes to the shed with the party, lays out the folder and goes back to the quay.

From the quay it is 10 minutes to the rock ledge or 5 minutes to the customs shed. Thyra Bøgh stays by the dinghy unless the party expressly asks her to come along. The dinghy, a 60-foot rope, a tarpaulin and a boathook can be borrowed free of charge; she wants the things back afterwards.

The fighter or another hero can ask the two quay guards to make a rescue rope ready. They do it without a check and without extra travel time for the party. The rope lies ready on the rock ledge 20 minutes after arrival; the guards do not fight in the caves and do not count as extra adventurers. It helps only if the ship is later wrecked, and it does not stop the beam by itself.

checks.success: During the ordinary conversation it is clear that Thyra Bøgh is ashamed of her part in the order. Mention it without threatening her, and she promises at once to testify in public; that gives Advantage on the party’s later attempt to persuade Gorm Krogh to accept a hearing.
checks.failure: No extra time is lost, but the promise to testify comes only if the party asks for it. The receipt and the route are still handed over without a check.

checks.success: In 1 minute the signal drawing is read: it is the beam itself that must be cut off. Note both the lever and the option of covering the lighthouse window as workable solutions.
checks.failure: Vibeke explains the drawing in 5 minutes in all. Both solutions are still open; no information is lost.

alternatives: Go straight to the rock ledge. Thyra Bøgh’s testimony gives the route they need; Halfdan and Gorm Krogh can tell the rest themselves.
Take the documents first, either on the quay or in the customs shed. They make the conversation at the mirror easier, but they require neither fighting nor paying.

Examine the outside of the lighthouse first: from the quay the path to the lighthouse door takes 10 minutes, and the unlocked stair to the lantern room another 5. The green beam comes up through a closed light shaft that no person can pass. A tarpaulin tied over the fixed frame of the lighthouse window stops the beam in 5 minutes without a check and holds for the rest of the night. That saves the ship but does not free Halfdan. From the lighthouse door to the rock ledge is 5 minutes; from the lantern room, add the 5 minutes back down.
scenes.dmNotes: Aim for 10–15 minutes of play on the quay. Give the necessary clues when the players ask about the cargo, the keeper or the drawing; never make checks the price of them. The receipt is signed on purpose: Gorm Krogh considers his revenge just and wanted his claim on record. Count only the time actually spent, not a fixed price for each point in this scene.

scenes.title: A Letter with Two Seals
scenes.summary: The documents show both Gorm Krogh’s crime and the wrong he wants to avenge. The scene is optional and can be played at Vibeke’s folder on the quay if the party asked for it there; the customs shed offers shelter and a place to work, not an artificial gate on information.
scenes.readAloud: In the folder, salt-stiff papers lie around a letter with two dark wax seals. Cinnamon dust sifts from a folded receipt, and a drawing shows a mirror on a tilting arm. A lone left shoe stands with its toe pressed against the folder’s strap. On the oldest page a family name has been scraped out and written in again.
details: A thorough search takes 5 minutes and yields all the documents without a check. Use the ready-to-print texts in the clue list: Halfdan’s work note names the Mirror Chamber and the stone behind the memorial stone; the pact letter says that Gorm Krogh pledged his living form; the old charter documents the family’s title of light reeve and the wish for an open hearing.

The charter in the folder is Vibeke’s certified copy, with impressions of the two seals. The original old letter is with Gorm Krogh in the Mirror Chamber. They are not two different rights: the copy can be used as evidence, while the original is the security he wants to keep in a peaceful agreement.

Vibeke approved the rebuilding from Gorm Krogh’s drawing without visiting the site. Her endorsement is on the copy. If it is brought up, she admits the mistake and lets the party show the papers in public. She can compare Gorm Krogh’s handwriting on the receipt and the pact without a check. If she has already gone back to the quay, the comparison is in her short margin note; the clues do not need her to be present.

On the inside of the folder’s cover Halfdan has sketched the safe position: lever all the way down means mirror towards the stone floor. A green beam in the light shaft means the mirror still points out through the lighthouse. The mechanism is purely mechanical; reading it correctly needs no spell.

The left shoe was found in the salvaged crate together with the mirror. Under the sole there is only a house mark, no writing. Vibeke says that three times it has come back to Halfdan’s doorstep after being put out on the quay; she borrowed it to examine it. The shoe is a small magical curiosity, not the key to the mirror. Its full, limited effect is listed under Treasure.

If the scene takes place in the customs shed, the walk here is 5 minutes from the quay, and the way on to the rock ledge 10 minutes. If the papers are examined on the quay, it is still only 10 minutes from the quay to the rock ledge. The documents and the shoe can be taken along by agreement; originals and borrowed belongings must go back to their owners.

checks.success: Within the 5-minute search both seals are recognised as valid. A hero can explain the old right of inheritance in concrete terms and gains Advantage on the attempt to negotiate with Gorm Krogh; several sources of Advantage do not add up.
checks.failure: The endorsement on the copy still establishes that the document is genuine. The party gets the proof, but not this extra Advantage. No extra time is lost.

checks.success: The search reveals that the resin binds the pact to the mirror’s beam, not to Halfdan’s life. Turning the lever down therefore does not harm him, and it does not turn those who are already undead back into living people.
checks.failure: The magical connection stays unclear, but the drawing still shows the safe mechanical solution. The party spends the same 5 minutes; no necessary clues are lost.

alternatives: Take the folder along and read it during the next conversation, somewhere sheltered. The documents need no particular place or locked reading room.
Skip the scene. Gorm Krogh has the original letter himself, and Halfdan can explain the lever from where he is held; the peaceful solution is still possible.
A wizard can use magic to examine or illuminate the papers under the spell’s normal rules. No false curse punishes reading the evidence.
scenes.dmNotes: Spend no more than 10–15 minutes of play here. Hand out the documents and let the players draw the conclusion; they need not pass a test to call a signed order evidence. Show Gorm Krogh’s rightful claim alongside his guilt, so that the negotiation becomes a choice, not a hidden answer key.

scenes.title: The Names in the Salt Stone
scenes.summary: A desecrated memorial stone hides the maintenance passage and a sound shaft through to Halfdan. Five drowned guards want their burial respected; the party can pass with a simple rite, sneak by or fight.
scenes.readAloud: On the rock ledge five green-crusted coins lie scattered before a stone carved with rows of old names. A sailor with black seaweed at his collar stands among four salt-bleached skeletons. From a crack behind the stone come a hoarse voice and the sound of metal on metal. Above you the green light cuts out over the surf.
details: Thyra Bøgh’s directions, Halfdan’s note or an ordinary look at the left side of the stone reveals the pressure stone without a check. Press it in, and a low door opens into the maintenance passage. No key is needed. The passage turns down and around beneath the lighthouse; the way to the Mirror Chamber takes 5 minutes. The short sound shaft runs straight through the rock, so Halfdan can be heard even though the walkable route is longer.

Halfdan can answer through the crack. He says that he is chained to the mirror’s turning gear, that Gorm Krogh turned wax-grey when the resin burned, and that the signet ring stayed on his hand. He also says that the free tilt lever is out of his reach, and that Gorm Krogh is rehearsing a speech about his family’s title. All three pieces of information come without a check in the first short exchange.

The memorial stone is the old salvage roll, carved in stone. Gorm Krogh scattered the five grave coins to take the mirror; the coins still lie just in front of the stone. If all five are put back in their small hollows, OR the five rows on the stone are read aloud with respect, the guards step aside without a check. The players can simply declare that the names are read; the GM need not invent five new named people. Putting the memorial in order takes 5 minutes. The guards do not attack anyone who begins the rite peacefully.

There is exactly one drowned sailor with the Ghast stat block and four drowned oarsmen with the Skeleton stat block. They stand here to prevent more grave robbing. They do not open with an attack: the sailor points at the coins and then at the stone. A fight begins if the party attacks or tries to force its way past the guards without answering, sneaking or bargaining to put the stone right.

Outside there is enough dusk light to see the stone, the guards and the tracks. Inside, the Mirror’s Breath applies, whose rules are gathered at the Mirror Chamber: hand-held nonmagical light goes out after one minute; magical light works, and the reflected green light gives Dim Light. The passage holds no damage and no secret penalty round by round.

If the quay guards were asked for help, the promised rescue rope lies here 20 minutes after arrival. Thyra Bøgh is still by the dinghy unless the party brought her along; she need not be present for the rite or the door.

checks.success: A group check lets the party slip behind the memorial stone under the crash of the waves. The passage takes the normal 5 minutes to the Mirror Chamber; there is no extra hidden time cost.
checks.failure: The guards spot the party, point at the scattered coins and block the door. The attempt has cost 5 minutes. The party can still put the memorial in order peacefully; a fight starts only if they try to push past.

checks.success: The cleric or another knowledgeable hero can point out in 1 minute where the five coins belong, so the rite takes only 1 minute in all.
checks.failure: The hollows visibly fit the coins. The rite still works without danger, but it takes the normal 5 minutes in all.

encounter.tactics: The drowned sailor blocks the low door and uses the Ghast stat block’s normal melee attacks and traits. The four oarsmen shoot their ordinary bows from the sides of the stone, or close to melee if pressed. Both kinds of guard stay on the solid rock ledge. They stop fighting at once if someone begins putting the five coins back and the rest of the party stops attacking; a willing retreat to the cliff path is not pursued.
encounter.terrain: A rock ledge 30 feet wide with the memorial stone in the middle. The solid path lies behind the party; the low opening of the passage is behind the stone. The stone gives Half Cover. The sea’s edge is plain to see, 10 feet from the fight; no automatic shoving or wave rules are added.

alternatives: Put the coins back or read the names respectfully, without a check. It is a complete solution, not a way of putting off the same fight.
Use Turn Undead or other magic under the normal rules. If the guards are driven off, the opening of the passage is clear; they do not magically follow the party into the next scene.

Go back to the lighthouse’s unlocked outer door and cover the window. From the rock ledge it is 5 minutes to the lighthouse door and 5 minutes up to the lantern room; fastening the tarpaulin takes 5 minutes without a check. That solution saves the ship but does not free Halfdan.
scenes.dmNotes: The fight is 450 + 4×50 = 650 XP, within the normal budget. A peaceful passage is just as complete. Avoid using a failed sneak as a forced Initiative roll. If the party has already put out the light at the lighthouse window, the guards still want the memorial put in order, but there is no longer any time pressure from the ship.

scenes.title: The Hand on the Lever
scenes.summary: Halfdan and Gorm Krogh stand on either side of the bronze mirror’s turning gear. The party can save the ship with a single mechanical action that is within reach, and then end the captivity by negotiation, guile or combat; Gorm Krogh’s guilt and his family’s right of inheritance are two separate questions.
scenes.readAloud: A bronze mirror fills the back wall of the cave and sends green light up a narrow shaft. Halfdan sits by the frame with a short chain around his ankle; his fingertips cannot reach the tilt lever. Opposite him stands a wax-grey man with a signet ring and a sealed letter in his belt, salt water dripping from his sleeves. Burnt cinnamon stings your nose, and four more undead stand silent along the wet wall.
details: The objective: Physical route: lever the chain’s rusty wall bracket free with a crowbar or a sturdy bar; a DC 12 Strength (Athletics) check takes 1 minute. On a success Halfdan is free. On a failure the bracket is still stuck and the work has cost 5 minutes in all; the attempt can be repeated. Instead, the lock can be opened with thieves’ tools and a DC 12 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, with the same time and the same result on a failure, or with Gorm Krogh’s key without a check. Without a fight: show Gorm Krogh the proof of his family’s title, or let him read his letter aloud himself, and promise a public hearing of his case. A DC 12 Charisma (Persuasion) check makes him hand over the key; on a failure he will still do so if a hero signs the promise and lets him keep the original letter as security. The conversation takes 5 minutes, even on a failure. Once freed, Halfdan turns the tilt lever down at once, without a check; the party can also reach and turn it themselves while he is still chained. It takes an action, stops the beam and causes no damage. The normal light can be lit 10 minutes later. If the party only stops the beam, the ship is saved, but Halfdan must still be freed. When the deadline runs out, the ship strikes the reef if the beam still points out to sea; Halfdan does not die automatically and can be rescued afterwards.

Halfdan is awake and can walk once freed. Gorm Krogh is the wax-grey man; introduce him by his full name when he demands to be heard. He has the key, the original letter and an ordinary sword. The other guards are one drowned mate and three drowned steersmen; they are not the guards the party met on the rock ledge.

Gorm Krogh opens with talk: he holds out the letter and wants to know whether anyone dares promise him a public hearing. The letter is genuine. A copy, Thyra Bøgh’s promise to testify or his own reading aloud can all be used; no item from the customs shed is an absolute requirement. He admits to the receipt and the transformation if confronted with the evidence. He calls the wreck necessary leverage, not an accident.

Peaceful solution: promise a public hearing at which the family’s letter is read. A DC 12 Charisma (Persuasion) check makes Gorm Krogh hand over the key. On a failure he will still do so if a hero signs the promise and lets him keep the original letter as security. Paper and charcoal lie by the mirror. The whole conversation takes 5 minutes, even on a failure. An agreement is not forgiveness for his crime; it binds the party to get the case heard.

Physical release: a crowbar or a sturdy bar under the chain’s rusty wall bracket calls for a DC 12 Strength (Athletics) check. A success takes 1 minute and frees Halfdan; on a failure the bracket is still stuck and the attempt has cost 5 minutes in all. The lock can be opened with thieves’ tools and a DC 12 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, with exactly the same time cost and the same result on a failure. Attempts may be repeated. Gorm Krogh’s key or a Knock spell opens the lock in the normal way, without this check.

The tilt lever is freely reachable on the side of the frame facing the door, 15 feet from the entrance. Anyone who reaches it can spend an action to turn it all the way down, with no check, no key, no damage and no need to kill anyone first. The mirror then faces the stone floor, and the green beam stops for good. Once freed, Halfdan does the same at once if nobody else has already done it. The light does not come back on as a surprise. Gorm Krogh may still be angry, but the mechanism robs him of his leverage.

A tarpaulin over the lighthouse window also counts as a stopped beam, even though the mirror still shines inside. The magic on the hand lanterns ends only when the mirror is turned down. Putting out the light does not change Gorm Krogh back into a living man and does not harm Halfdan; it is expressly not a hidden trap.

If the beam is stopped before 90 minutes, the ship comes clear of the reef. Otherwise the wreck happens exactly at the deadline; the cargo is lost and eight sailors take refuge on the afterdeck. Halfdan can still be rescued. Once he is free and the mirror is turned down, he can light the normal light in 10 minutes by an inner service stair, without a check. That counts after the stop already achieved, not as a new requirement for saving the ship.

If the party attacks Gorm Krogh, the fight below begins. The guards do not attack during honest negotiation. If a hero turns the lever first, all the undead pause for a moment; the party can offer the same hearing at once. If the party refuses and keeps attacking, Gorm Krogh fights alongside the guards. There is no need to kill him to make the ship safe.

encounter.tactics: Gorm Krogh uses the Wight stat block’s normal weapons and abilities and tries to keep enemies at bay; he gains no control of the mirror as an extra monster power. The mate fights in melee with the Ghast stat block’s normal traits. The three steersmen shoot their ordinary bows from the back wall or join the melee. No one attacks Halfdan or breaks the lever as a hidden punishment. Gorm Krogh accepts the offer of a hearing even in the middle of the fight if the party stops attacking. After his surrender or defeat the others lay down their weapons if the party promises to put the memorial stone in order; they do not follow fleeing heroes out onto the cliff path.
encounter.terrain: A 40×30-foot chamber. The entrance is in the middle of the south wall; the frame and the lever stand 15 feet inside. Halfdan is on the east side of the frame; Gorm Krogh stands by the north wall, 15 feet behind the lever. A clear passage 5 feet wide runs along each side of the frame. The frame gives Half Cover. There are no hidden pits, automatic shoves or extra wave rules.
encounter.hazard: The Mirror’s Breath. When: whenever a hand-held, nonmagical torch or lantern has burned for 1 minute in the maintenance passage or the Mirror Chamber while the mirror points up the light shaft; each relighting starts its own minute. Targets: only these light sources, not people or other objects. Save: none. Effect: the flame goes out; no damage or condition. The reflected green light still gives Dim Light. Counter: magical light works normally, and turning the mirror’s tilt lever down ends the effect. Screening the lighthouse window saves the ship but does not end this effect inside.

alternatives: Turn the lever first. That makes the ship safe without settling every conflict; the rescue and Gorm Krogh’s fate can then be decided without the ship’s clock.
Negotiate, show evidence or let Gorm Krogh read his own original. If the attempt to persuade him fails, the written promise gives a sure way on without another roll of the dice.

Hide the party’s intent during the conversation and let someone else walk around the frame; the lever is visible and free, and ordinary movement and actions apply. Magic follows the normal spells; there is no unwritten immunity to creative problem-solving.

Fall back to fetch a bar, tools or help. The route to the rock ledge takes 5 minutes, and to the quay another 10. A beam that has already been stopped does not restart, but a running clock keeps running during the trip.
scenes.dmNotes: The climax is 700 + 450 + 3×50 = 1300 XP if it comes to a fight. Halfdan is a prisoner, not an extra foe or a source of XP. A peaceful solution is a full victory. The quick route, with the talk on the quay, the direct walk, the rite, the passage and the negotiation, takes about 30 minutes; by way of the customs shed about 40. A Short Rest of 60 minutes is therefore a visibly risky choice, not a hidden trap. Decide the ship’s fate by the actual time, and let a later rescue still make a difference.

npcs.name: Gorm Krogh
npcs.role: Transformed town councillor, the adventure’s adversary
npcs.look: A wax-grey face, a stiff council robe and a signet ring on a finger where the skin has begun to slip. Salt water drips from his sleeves even when he stands in the dry.
npcs.personality: Formal, proud and aggrieved; he mistakes a just cause for the right to hurt others.
npcs.wants: A promise, spoken aloud, that his family’s old letter will be read before an open council. He will not settle for being proved right in a cave where no one else can hear it.
npcs.secret: He knew that the mirror’s pact would cost him his living form, but believed the threat of a single wreck would be enough. His fear of having made a mistake that cannot be undone makes a concrete offer of a hearing stronger than a threat.
npcs.voice: Speaks as if at a council meeting, straightens up and smooths his robe. “Read the letter first. Then you may call me whatever you like.” When anyone mentions the sailors, he looks away from the mirror.
npcs.where: The Hand on the Lever, in the Mirror Chamber by the turning gear. The key and the original letter hang at his belt.

npcs.name: Halfdan
npcs.role: Captive lighthouse keeper, the one the party must rescue
npcs.look: Streaks of soot across his cheek, a salt-stiff wool jersey and a raw chafe at the ankle chain. He holds an iron bar that is too short in both hands.
npcs.personality: Practical and stubborn. Talks about the ship and the mechanism first, then about himself.
npcs.wants: To get the mirror turned down and to get free, so that he can light the normal light again.
npcs.secret: He found Gorm Krogh’s old letter and gave him permission himself to examine the salvaged crate. He fears his own goodwill will be mistaken for complicity, but he tells the truth if asked.
npcs.voice: Short, hoarse and precise. “The lever first. All the way down. My foot can wait a moment.” Points with the bar instead of making speeches.
npcs.where: The Hand on the Lever, chained in the Mirror Chamber; can also be heard through the sound shaft at The Names in the Salt Stone. He is not physically in two places.

npcs.name: Thyra Bøgh
npcs.role: Smuggler, eyewitness and the rogue’s old contact
npcs.look: Tar on her thumb, grains of resin under her nails and a jar of pickled onions stuffed into a roomy coat pocket.
npcs.personality: Straightforward once the danger is real; evasive about money and customs duty. She would rather help with a boat than with an apology.
npcs.wants: For Halfdan to come home, and for her dinghy to still be hers once her testimony is given.
npcs.secret: She read the line in the order about the reef and let the money do the talking anyway. She cannot honestly claim that she suspected nothing, but she will help stop the crime.
npcs.voice: Bites an onion in half between sentences and wipes her fingers on her coat. “I fetched a crate. That was stupid. I’ll help you put it right.”
npcs.where: The Wrong Course, by the dinghy on Ugletoft’s quay. Stays there unless the party asks her to come along.

npcs.name: Vibeke
npcs.role: Harbour clerk, document expert and the wizard’s professional sparring partner
npcs.look: An ink-blue fingerprint on the tip of her nose, and a folder with dry leather flaps around salt-stiff papers.
npcs.personality: Meticulous on paper, less sure in the field. Likes to be right, but corrects her mistake when the proof lies in front of her.
npcs.wants: To save the ship and get the case on record before anyone burns the letters or makes the wrong person the scapegoat.
npcs.secret: She approved the rebuilding from a drawing. Her signature is on the copy, so she will not give the party a false explanation if they ask her directly.
npcs.voice: Taps once on the line that matters. “This is a signature, not a rumour.” Grows calmer when someone takes her documents seriously.
npcs.where: The Wrong Course, on the quay with key and folder. She can come along to A Letter with Two Seals in the customs shed and then returns to the quay; the scene can also be played at the folder on the quay.

rewards.name: The Harbour’s Rescue Reward
rewards.where: Vibeke pays it from the harbour’s rescue fund once the party is back at the quay.
rewards.description: A canvas bag of stamped harbour coins: 80 gp for bringing Halfdan home alive and 80 gp for keeping the cargo ship clear of the reef. Both together give 160 gp; if only one goal is achieved, 80 gp is paid. The reward depends on the rescue, not on killing Gorm Krogh.

rewards.name: The Smuggler’s Silver Cup
rewards.where: Thyra Bøgh gives it from the dinghy’s locked locker if the party brings Halfdan back alive.
rewards.description: A dented silver cup engraved with a wave pattern. Thyra Bøgh calls it her share of the rescue money and keeps only the dinghy and her promise to testify. The cup is not another piece of evidence or a hidden curse.

rewards.name: The Shoe That Walks Home
rewards.where: Examined at Vibeke’s folder during A Letter with Two Seals
rewards.description: A lone left shoe with a crooked seam and a house mark under the sole; a magical curiosity made for this adventure, not an SRD item. At sunset, if it lies loose no more than 1 mile from Halfdan’s doorstep on the quay, it walks 5 feet per round by the shortest passable route back there; it cannot open doors, climb, carry anything or break free of a hand or a container, and out of range it lies still.

endings.success: If the green beam is stopped or covered before 90 minutes and Halfdan is freed, the ship stays clear of the reef. Halfdan lights the normal light 10 minutes after he is both free and has turned the mirror down; that delay does not undo the rescue already won. Vibeke prepares a public hearing if the party promised one, and Thyra Bøgh can testify about the order. Gorm Krogh’s documented right of inheritance is dealt with separately from his crime. If he was spared, he remains undead and must be guarded while the case goes on; if he was defeated, the letter can still be read. The party earns rewards for the goals they achieved.
endings.partial: Settle the two goals separately. If the beam was stopped before 90 minutes but Halfdan is still a prisoner, the ship is safe, and the party can go back for the keeper without the clock restarting. If Halfdan is free but the beam was only stopped at or after 90 minutes, the ship is already on the reef: the cargo is lost, and eight sailors are waiting to be rescued. Use the rescue option below. A later release or rescue still counts; there is no unwritten execution of Halfdan.
endings.failure: If the beam still reaches the sea at 90 minutes and Halfdan has not been freed, the hull splits on the reef while the keeper stays a prisoner. Gorm Krogh gets his wreck, but not, by that alone, the council’s consent or power over the whole town. Vibeke and Thyra Bøgh try to bring the eight sailors ashore and ask the party for help. The evidence, the prisoner and the mirror do not vanish because time ran out; rescue and justice can still be pursued, but the cargo is lost, and the town remembers the delay.

unexpected.trigger: The party goes straight to the lighthouse and covers the window instead of following the clues down into the caves.
unexpected.response: Let it work. From the quay the path to the lighthouse door takes 10 minutes and the unlocked stair up 5 minutes. A tarpaulin tied fast over the frame of the lighthouse window takes another 5 minutes without a check and holds for the rest of the night. The light shaft is too narrow for people. The ship is now safe, but Halfdan is still a prisoner; do not undo the solution by sending them after some other beam. From the lighthouse door it is 5 minutes to the rock ledge, and from the lantern room add the 5 minutes back down.

unexpected.trigger: The party arrests or drives off Thyra Bøgh before getting her testimony.
unexpected.response: The receipt is in her coat pocket and is handed over in an open conversation or a lawful search within the story; she does not try to swallow it. Vibeke’s drawing, Halfdan’s work note and the voice at the memorial stone are independent clues. Violence can cost the party her willing help, but it must not remove every route to Halfdan.

unexpected.trigger: The party wants to destroy the mirror or the turning gear in combat rather than use the lever.
unexpected.response: Describe the thin support bolt under the mirror’s tilting arm: AC 15, 10 HP, immune to Poison and Psychic damage. If the bolt breaks, the mirror tips forward towards the stone floor and stops the beam without any explosive damage; Halfdan’s chain is fixed to the frame’s solid foot and does not crush him. A cloth fastened over the mirror’s face also works, but the lever remains the quick, harmless solution.

unexpected.trigger: Gorm Krogh is killed before anyone has heard his explanation.
unexpected.response: The key and the original letter are still on his belt, found without a check. Halfdan can tell of the transformation, and Vibeke’s copies keep the trail of the stolen title. His death does not stop the mirror by itself; the visible tilting arm does. If the party promised a hearing, the promise can still be kept by presenting the letter and hearing the witnesses.

unexpected.trigger: The party gives up at the deadline, or wants to rescue the crew after the wreck.
unexpected.response: The eight sailors are on a stable afterdeck 50 feet from the rock ledge. With the 60-foot rope made ready and the quay guards, all of them can be hauled across in 20 minutes without a check. If the rope was not made ready, Thyra Bøgh’s dinghy and a boathook can be used for three careful trips along the lee side; that takes 30 minutes once boat and help are there. Trips to fetch gear use the travel times already given. The cargo is lost, but none of the eight dies automatically during this rescue; avoid inventing a new hidden clock.

unexpected.trigger: The party wants to wait, rest or leave town altogether.
unexpected.response: Show the ship’s course and give the known travel times. A Short Rest takes 1 hour and uses up the real time remaining; the green beam can be dealt with first, so that a rest becomes a sensible choice. If the party leaves town with the beam still active, the wreck happens 90 minutes after their original arrival. If they leave after screening it, the ship stays safe, while Halfdan and Gorm Krogh still need a resolution.

tips: Write 0, 30, 60 and 90 on a scrap of paper. Tell the players how long a visible route or a longer attempt will take before they choose. Combat counts in rounds; the 10 minutes it takes to relight the lighthouse after the rescue do not count against the deadline for stopping the beam.
Hand out the documents when the party examines them. Never let a failed History or Arcana check make a clear signature unreadable. A spare clue is a blessing when the party skips the customs shed.

Open both possible fights with a situation the players can read: the drowned point at the coins, and Gorm Krogh offers the letter. A peaceful solution is as final as a won fight; do not call up new foes to fill the XP budget.
Keep three questions apart: Is the ship safe? Is Halfdan free? How are Gorm Krogh’s crime and his family’s old claim to be handled? One can succeed even if the others do not.

For a short session the document folder can be examined on the quay and the memorial put in order with a brief declaration. Keep the decisions and the evidence; cut repeated explanations rather than squeezing four scenes in as four compulsory fights.
sequelHooks: During the promised hearing a gap turns up in the harbour’s old accounts on the very day the title of light reeve changed hands. Vibeke asks the party to fetch the missing ledger from a warehouse before a public auction scatters the estate.

Thyra Bøgh offers to show where the bronze mirror was salvaged. The wreck’s cargo list mentions a sealed chest that her people left behind because knocking came from inside it at low tide; the party can look into it only once Halfdan and the harbour’s present crisis are safe.
